data: Stanford COVID-19 wearables phase 1 (Mishra et al. 2020) and phase 2 subset (Alavi et al. 2022)

method_labels.fusion: Personal baseline, CUSUM and multivariate fused

cohort.sampling_note: Phase 1: 120 recordings from 118 people (one person has three short recordings, all excluded for length). Phase 2 is a subset of the release: all 84 positives, plus the first 60 Fitbit and first 60 other-device participant IDs in sorted order (not a random draw). Dates are shifted per person by the data owners, so pretend events cannot be matched to the calendar: lockdowns and isolation after a positive test are tangled up with onset.

ppv.assumption: Illness rate 0.97 per person-year (upper-respiratory symptoms on the ISS, DOMAIN ref 52b); sensitivity = detection net of luck on real data.

rhr_act7.label: Resting heart rate + 7-day mean of steps

like_for_like_real.label: Symptom-dated episodes of the validation half, resting heart rate + 7-day mean activity

rhr_rhrday_steps.label: Night and whole-day resting heart rate + steps (exploratory, added after seeing the main result)

rhr_steps_adjusted.label: … + adjust heart rate for the previous day's steps

sleep_subset.note: Only the phase 1 COVID-19 participants have sleep files, so nobody in this subset is illness-free and the false-alert estimate rests on little quiet time.

deployed_config.label: Model and thresholds from the simulator, heart rate + 7-day activity, applied unchanged to real people

import_model_on_vendor_rhr.source: LifeSnaps, Fitbit's own daily resting heart rate (no illness labels: every alert counted)

shipped_model.label: The model file the app ships (11 indicators, thresholds from simulated missions), given the channels a real import shares with it: overnight heart rate and, where recorded, sleep duration

chance_note: Pretend events are placed on label-quiet days with the same missing data as real windows, and weighted to the device mix of the real episodes. They cannot be matched to the calendar (dates are shifted per person), so exposure, travel, testing and isolation near a real onset are not reproduced; detection above luck is therefore an upper bound on what physiology alone explains.

published.source: Mishra et al. 2020 (DOMAIN.md ref 58), phase 1 only, their own online CuSum on hourly data
published.note: Different features, protocol and people subset; shown for orientation, not as a like-for-like comparison.
